title: Universal tooling adapters for typed function calls and resilient streaming invocations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: SDK users in Python/TS/Go are having inconsistent experiences when using tool/function-calling features across runtimes: validation errors surface at request time with poor messages, streaming invocations lack stable resume semantics, and retries either double-invoke side effects or are disabled due to ambiguous idempotency. Goal: provide a set of cross-SDK adapters that provide (1) deterministic JSON schema validation with developer-friendly diagnostics, (2) typed conversion helpers and argument coercion for Python/TS/Go, (3) a streaming invocation wrapper with resume tokens and at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics guidance, and (4) a retry orchestration helper that understands function idempotency metadata and can safely retry streaming and non-streaming calls.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable validation adapter exists in each SDK that consumes a JSON Schema-like function descriptor and returns normalized args or clear error diagnostics
SDKs expose a small "InvocationHelper" API (names may vary per language) that supports sync/async, streaming, and provides a resume token when streaming is interrupted

Retry helper consults function metadata (idempotent: true|false|safe-retry-window) and applies exponential backoff with jitter; tests show no duplicated side effects in simulated non-idempotent function when window disabled
End-to-end example app added for each SDK (python, typescript, go) demonstrating: validation errors, streaming resume after network glitch, and safe retry behavior with mock remote tools
Docs page and API reference added to SDK docs with examples and migration guidance
Unit and integration tests added covering edge cases (extra fields, nested optional objects, binary blobs, streaming reconnect with partial chunks)
implementation_notes: Language-specific decisions: use pydantic-lite validation for Python (no heavy runtime deps), zod in TypeScript, and a small hand-written validator for Go to avoid large schema libraries

Validation approach: accept function descriptor expressed as simple typed JSON (name, required args, arg types, idempotency metadata, examples). Generate diagnostics that include path, expected type, and a suggested coercion (e.g. '123' -> 123).

Invocation helper should wrap lower-level SDK call loop and inject: argument normalization, pre-call simulation hook (for dry-run unit tests), structured logging with token/trace IDs, and post-call verification for retries

Streaming wrapper: maintain an opaque resume_token returned by runtime. On disconnect, the SDK should call /resume with token and provide the caller an iterator that yields only new events. If server does not support resume, fallback to replay with a warning and an idempotency guard

Retries: implement a RetryPolicy object that encodes max_attempts, backoff(base, max), and idempotency_strategy (always, never, within_window). The SDK should honor user-provided idempotency keys for functions that have side effects
Backward compatibility: keep the existing simple call surface (Client.callFunction) unchanged; introduce opt-in helpers to be adopted by teams progressively
Telemetry: add structured counters for validation failures, resume success/failure, retry attempts, and duplicate-invocation detections for enterprise customers
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Scoped API surface and wrote initial design doc in Confluence (link below). Discussed trade-offs between full JSON-Schema vs lightweight descriptor with the SDK leads; consensus to avoid full JSON-Schema due to complexity in Go.
2025-02-25: Implemented prototype validator in Python (pydantic-free) and TS (zod). Basic coercion tests pass for primitives and nested objects. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1182

2025-02-27: Spike on streaming resume semantics completed. Ran a local server that returned resume_token for mid-stream disconnects; Python/TS clients can recover and resume without data duplication in most cases. Need to formalize server-side resume contract.

2025-03-01: Design review with runtime team — agreed to add explicit resume_token field to runtime response envelope and a 'resume_supported' flag per model endpoint. Runtime will add feature flag 'fn-resume-v1' under canary environments.

2025-03-03: Began Go validator implementation; discovered edge cases for union types and bytes encoding. Chose base64 canonicalization for binary blobs to keep cross-language consistency. Added tests for base64 round-trip.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay particular attention to the provided code examples for edge-case behavior (see implementation_notes). We need sign-off on the resume semantics and the idempotency strategy before merging runtime changes. Especially validate that the fallback replay path includes enough metadata for downstream duplicate-detection.
